title: Ring Dip
summary: A dip on gymnastic rings, which are unstable, so the chest, triceps and shoulders work harder than on bars and the bottom stretch is deeper.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for chest (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly chest total.
Library rating 1 for triceps (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly triceps total.
Library rating 0.5 for front delts (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly front delts total.
Library rating 0.15 for abs: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly abs total.

setup.text: Support yourself on the rings with your arms straight and the rings turned slightly out.
Lower until your shoulders are just below your elbows, keeping the rings close to your body.
Press back up to straight arms.

form_cues.cue: Lower until shoulders are below elbows
Keep the rings close to your body
Learn the support hold first. If the rings shake, stick with bar dips for now.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.
